text:
alex_oncall: paging: alerting spike across canary region eu-west-2 after today's rollout. errors ~5% 5xx on /v1/generate. getting paged by alerting.
deploy-bot: Deploy started by maya_eng at 2024-07-10T14:34:14Z for rollout/feature/fast-token-cache (4 hosts canary)
alex_oncall: i'm checking logs now, seeing KV cache misses + OOM traces on two GPUs. latency spikes 2-3x for affected requests. tag me if you want traces.
jamie_sre: thx. are these only canary hosts or broader? initial metric shows request success rate for canary pool down to 94.6%, prod stable at 99.9% so far.
maya_eng: canary-only for now. we merged a single commit that touched allocator heuristics + cache warm path. suspect that change.
lin_product: any visible customer impact? CS reported a few API errors from an EU customer a minute ago. pinged them to gather sample ids.
alex_oncall: customer_ops, do you have the request ids? we need to correlate.
customer_ops: shared 3 sample request IDs in thread DM to alex_oncall. they failed with 503, model returned "internal_error".
jamie_sre: let's flip the kill-switch for the feature-flag controlling the new cache behavior on canary only. maya, can you patch the flag? otherwise i'll route canary traffic to fallback pool.
maya_eng: on it. Pushing a flag rollback now: /ops/flags toggle token-cache-heuristic=false --scope=canary --no-wait
ops-bot: Flag toggle requested by maya_eng: token-cache-heuristic=false (scope: canary). Waiting for confirmation from deploy admin.
alex_oncall: i can confirm once the flag hits all canary hosts. i'm tailing canary logs.
maya_eng: confirmed flag rolled out to 4/4 hosts in canary at 14:41:03Z.
jamie_sre: i'm seeing success rate climb back to 99.8% in canary. latency back down. good sign.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout aborted and traffic routed to stable pool by jamie_sre at 14:42:10Z.
alex_oncall: paging clear for now. marking as mitigated. leaving thread open for RCA and decision on whether to revert the single commit or push a small hotfix.
maya_eng: quick context: that single commit introduced a cache allocation threshold that tries to keep < N buffer objects resident; under certain request size distributions it triggers extra allocations concurrently and spikes memory pressure. fix is trivial but i'd prefer a single-commit revert to be safest.
lin_product: if we revert, will there be behavioral differences customers notice? any regresison risks?
maya_eng: no functional change for stable path. only affects cache aggressiveness. revert will restore prior heuristics.
jamie_sre: ops: recommend revert the single commit and run a limited canary (2 hosts) then promote. also prepare a small patch with added safety checks for longer term.
alex_oncall: i'm going to open a follow-up ticket: INC-1719987654 with timeline + customer ids + metric graphs.
customer_ops: i've proactively notified the impacted customer with a short note: we observed transient errors in EU canary, mitigation applied, we're rolling back change and will follow up with root cause and ETA.
maya_eng: creating revert PR now. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/12345 revert: allocator/cache-heuristic (single commit)
deploy-bot: PR 12345 opened by maya_eng. CI checks queued.
jamie_sre: i'll prep the rollback playbook and sit on the deploy channel. oncall escalation: @eng-oncall please standby for verification after CI green.
maya_eng: CI passed. i'm scheduling a hotfix revert canary at 15:02:00Z with deploy pipeline 'hotpatch-small'.
deploy-bot: Hotpatch deploy (revert PR 12345) started by maya_eng. Targets: 2 canary hosts -> then gradual promote.
alex_oncall: watching metrics. will announce on this thread when canary looks healthy.
maya_eng: canary finished and graduated. revert promoted at 15:07:18Z.
jamie_sre: saw no regressions. success rate and latency stable. marking post-deploy verification complete.
customer_ops: updated customer with rollback confirmation and offered to share postmortem once ready. they appreciate the prompt response.
alex_oncall: handing off to jamie_sre for incident follow-up and RCA. i'm going offshift in 20m. leaving notes in ticket.
jamie_sre: thanks alex. i'll own RCA, include timeline, diff analysis, and propose two mitigations: (1) revert + tighter canary gating automated (2) add safety guard in allocator with fallback to old path on mem pressure. also schedule a postmortem review with eng team tomorrow.
maya_eng: ack. i'll prepare patch that adds a guard and unit tests to avoid this landing again.
lin_product: please also add a short customer-facing summary for CS+AM teams.
jamie_sre: will do. closing incident thread once postmortem doc linked. final status: mitigated, rollback applied, no ongoing customer degradation.
ops-bot: Incident INC-1719987654 created and assigned to jamie_sre. Severity: Sev2. Timeline recorded.
alex_oncall: thanks everyone. great coordination. :thumbsup:
maya_eng: thanks — i'll follow up with PR for the guard today.
jamie_sre: assigning to morning retro and RCA doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/incident/INC-1719987654/postmortem
